title_en: Al-Ashari's Creed and His Retraction of It
body_ar:
بعض الناس يقول إن عقيدة الأشعري غير صحيحة و أنه تراجع عنها قبل موته فما صحة ذلك؟

أن الإمام أبا الحسن علي بن إسماعيل الأشعري إمام من أئمة أهل السنة من المسلمين و هو من ذرية أبي موسى صاحب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم و قد اشتهر بحفظ الكتاب و السنة و إتقان علوم الدين و كان قد رأى أن الاجتهاد الذي وضعت فيه المذاهب اقتصر على الجانب الفقهي و لم يصل إلى الجانب العقدي فأراد أن يضع قواعد للمسلمين في العقيدة تكون مذهبا و قد كان في البداية على مذهب المعتزلة فرجع عنه و تاب منه و رد عليهم بكثير من الردود و كتبه في ذلك موجودة منتشرة

ثم لما وضع تلك القواعد كان منها بعض الإجتهادات الخاطئة التي هو مثاب عليها قطعا لأنه عرف منه الصلاح و الورع فما أصاب فيه فله فيه أجران و ما أخطأ فيه فله به أجر و تلك الأخطاء التي وقع فيها قد صرح هو برجوعه عنها في كتابه (مقالات الإسلاميين) و في كتابه (الإبانة عن أصول الديانة) و كلاهما مروي بالأسانيد المتصلة إلى المؤلف و قد ألف كذلك الحافظ بن عساكر كتابا سماه الذب عن الأشعري و هو كتاب مطبوع موجود

فلهذا يعلم أن أبا الحسن قد رجع عن تلك الأخطاء التي وقع فيها و من رجع عن الخطإ فإنه لا يعد محسوبا عليه و بالأخص أن المذهب الذي ينسبه الناس إلى الأشعري كثير من مسائله لم يسمع بها الأشعري و لا قالها ولا وجدت في زمانه و لا في شيء من كتبه و إنما قالها المتأخرون من المتكلمين و إذا راجعتم كتب العقائد المؤلفة على ما يسمى بالمذهب الأشعري ستجدون أنهم يقولون خلافا للشيخ أبي الحسن و بعض الأقوال تنسب إليه فينكرها بعض الأشاعرة أنفسهم

و لذلك قال السيوطي رحمه الله في الكوكب الساطع: يمتنع التقليد في العقائـــــــــد و العنبري جوزه و قد حظر ثم على الأول إن يقلــــــــــــــد لكن أبو هاشم لم يعتبــــــــــر قال القشيري عليه مفتـــــــرى الفخر و الأستاذ ثم الآمدي أسلافنا كالشافعي به النظـــــــــر فمؤمن عاص على المعتمـــــد إيمانه وقد عزي للأشعــــــــــري

فكثير من الأقوال التي تنسب إلى الأشعري لم يقل بها و أسانيدها غير صحيحة و لا توجد في شيء من كتبه أصلا و كثير منها يصرح أصحابه بأنهم خالفوا الشيخ أبا الحسن في ذلك كإثبات المعنويات الصفات السبع التي اشتهرت بالمعنويات أول من أثبتها الفخر الرازي و قد قال فيها إنه يخالف الشيخ أبا الحسن في ذلك صرح هو أنه يخالف الشيخ أبا الحسن في ذلك

و لهذا قال الشيخ محمد المام رحمه الله: الاشْعَرِي الاحْوَالْ انْكَرْهَ وَ اْلفَخَرْ الرَّازِي حَــرَّرْهَ عَنْهَ صِفَاتْ الرَّحْمَنْ

فصاحب الفكرة هو الفخر الرازي و ليس الإمام أبا الحسن الأشعري فالأشعري إذن أنكر ذلك و على هذا فما ينسب إليه على أنه مذهب له مثل ما ينسب إلى الإمام مالك أنه مذهب له و كثير من الأقوال لم يقلها و لا هي في موطإه و لا في الكتب المروية عنه

و لهذا قال الدبوسي من الحنفية قال: إن الأقوال المنسوبة إلى الأئمة و الفقه المدون في الكتب ينبغي أن يراجع فما كان منه من اجتهاد المجتهدين أخذ به و ما كان من اجتهاد المقلدين رد عليهم فكيف يجتهدون و هم لا يدعون الاجتهاد. هذا كلام الدبوسي من أئمة الحنفية مع أنه مقلد.
body_en:
Some people say that al-Ashari's creed is not sound, and that he retracted it before his death. What is the truth of that?

Imam Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Ismail al-Ashari is one of the imams of the people of the sunnah among the Muslims. He is of the progeny of Abu Musa, the Companion of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he became renowned for memorising the Book and the sunnah and for mastery of the sciences of religion. He had seen that the independent reasoning by which the schools of law were laid down was confined to the juristic side and had not reached the creedal side, and so he wanted to lay down principles for the Muslims in creed which would constitute a school. In the beginning he had been upon the school of the Mutazilah, then he retracted it and repented of it and refuted them with many refutations, and his books on that exist and are in circulation.

Then, when he laid down those principles, among them were some mistaken exercises of reasoning, for which he is certainly rewarded, because righteousness and scrupulousness were known of him: what he got right, he has two rewards for; and what he got wrong, he has one reward for. Those errors into which he fell, he himself stated expressly that he had retracted, in his book Maqālāt al-Islāmiyyīn and in his book al-Ibānah ʿan Uṣūl al-Diyānah, both of which are transmitted with connected chains to the author. The ḥāfiẓ Ibn Asakir also composed a book which he called al-Dhabb ʿan al-Ashʿarī, which is a printed and extant book.

From this it is known that Abu al-Hasan retracted those errors into which he had fallen; and one who retracts an error is not reckoned answerable for it. This is all the more so since, of the school that people ascribe to al-Ashari, many of its questions al-Ashari never heard of and never held, and which did not exist in his time nor in any of his books — rather it was the later theologians who said them. If you look through the books of creed composed upon what is called the Ashari school, you will find them saying 'contrary to Shaykh Abu al-Hasan'; and some positions are ascribed to him which some of the Asharis themselves deny. That is why al-Suyuti, may God have mercy on him, said in al-Kawkab al-Sāṭiʿ: *Following a scholar in the doctrines of creed is impermissible, in the view of al-Fakhr, the Ustadh, and then al-Amidi; al-Anbari allowed it, while our predecessors, like al-Shafi'i, barred speculation in it. Then, on the first view, if he does follow a scholar, he is a sinful believer, on the relied-upon view; but Abu Hashim did not reckon his faith as faith, and this has been ascribed to al-Ashari. Al-Qushayri said: it is a fabrication against him.*

So many of the positions ascribed to al-Ashari he did not hold; their chains of transmission are not sound, and they are not found in any of his books at all. And of many of them, those who hold them state expressly that they have gone against Shaykh Abu al-Hasan in that — such as the affirming of the maʿnawiyyāt, the seven attributes that have become known as the maʿnawiyyāt. The first to affirm them was al-Fakhr al-Razi, and he said of them that he differs from Shaykh Abu al-Hasan in that; he himself stated expressly that he differs from Shaykh Abu al-Hasan in that.

That is why Shaykh Muhammad al-Mami, may God have mercy on him, said: *Al-Ashari denied the states; and al-Fakhr al-Razi drew out from them the attributes of the Merciful.*

So the originator of the idea is al-Fakhr al-Razi, not Imam Abu al-Hasan al-Ashari; al-Ashari, then, denied that. On this basis, what is ascribed to him as being his school is like what is ascribed to Imam Malik as being his school: many of the positions he did not hold, and they are neither in his Muwaṭṭaʾ nor in the books narrated from him.

That is why al-Dabusi, of the Hanafis, said: the positions ascribed to the imams, and the fiqh recorded in the books, ought to be reviewed — what of it comes from the independent reasoning of those qualified for it should be taken, and what comes from the reasoning of those who merely follow should be returned to them; for how can they exercise independent reasoning when they do not even claim to be qualified for it? These are the words of al-Dabusi, one of the imams of the Hanafis, even though he was himself a follower.

flags.arabic: al-Suyuti's lines as printed: يمتنع التقليد في العقائد / و العنبري جوزه و قد حظر / ثم على الأول إن يقلد / لكن أبو هاشم لم يعتبر / قال القشيري عليه مفترى / الفخر و الأستاذ ثم الآمدي / أسلافنا كالشافعي به النظر / فمؤمن عاص على المعتمد / إيمانه وقد عزي للأشعري
flags.context: the verse quotation in the middle of the answer
options: read as four and a half lines whose hemistichs the page has printed out of order, and translate by meaning (as done here)
translate the nine half-lines in the printed order
leave the verse untranslated and carry only the Sheikh's framing
flags.note: SOURCE / EXTRACTION DEFECT. The page prints all five first hemistichs and then the four second hemistichs — the flattening of a two-column layout, the same defect as in article 531 of this slice. Read in the printed order the verse is unintelligible. The pairing is confirmed by article 534 of this slice, where the same lines are printed in running order; note that 534 reads للفخر where this page reads الفخر, and فيه النظر where this page reads به النظر. body_ar preserves the printed order untouched; the English restores the pairing by sense.

flags.arabic: الاشْعَرِي الاحْوَالْ انْكَرْهَ وَ اْلفَخَرْ الرَّازِي حَــرَّرْهَ عَنْهَ صِفَاتْ الرَّحْمَنْ
flags.context: the line attributed to Shaykh Muhammad al-Mami
options: Al-Ashari denied the states; and al-Fakhr al-Razi drew out from them the attributes of the Merciful
Al-Ashari denied the states, which al-Fakhr al-Razi refined; from them come the attributes of the Merciful
Al-Ashari denied the states; al-Fakhr al-Razi established them, and from them the attributes of the Merciful
flags.note: Hassaniya verse, vowelled in the source in the Mauritanian manner, with the pronominal suffix ـهَ for ـها throughout. حَرَّرْهَ can be 'drew it out', 'worked it out' or 'established it', and عَنْهَ can attach either to al-Razi's act or to the attributes. The Sheikh's own prose immediately afterwards settles the substance — that the idea originates with al-Razi and not with al-Ashari — so the argument does not rest on the line alone. A reviewer who knows al-Mami's naẓm should fix the wording.

flags.arabic: كإثبات المعنويات الصفات السبع التي اشتهرت بالمعنويات أول من أثبتها الفخر الرازي
flags.context: the claim about the origin of the maʿnawī attributes
options: translate the historical claim exactly as given and flag it
translate and add a note on the standard account
translate with the term maʿnawiyyāt glossed in the body
flags.note: الصفات المعنوية — the seven 'attributes of state' (His being powerful, knowing, living, willing, hearing, seeing, speaking) as distinct from the seven maʿānī — are usually traced in the Ashari tradition to the doctrine of aḥwāl associated with Abu Hashim al-Jubbai and to the later Asharis generally, rather than to al-Fakhr al-Razi as the first to affirm them. The Sheikh's attribution is given here exactly as he states it, twice over, and has not been adjusted; the historical point is recorded rather than corrected, per style guide §11.

flags.arabic: إن عقيدة الأشعري غير صحيحة و أنه تراجع عنها قبل موته
options: publish with a preface from the Sheikh's office
hold from publication pending the Sheikh's office
publish as an ordinary item in the creed series
flags.note: EDITORIAL REVIEW ADVISED (style guide §12). Whether al-Ashari retracted, and what present-day Asharis owe to him, is a live and communally charged question, and this answer takes clear positions in it. Note that the Sheikh's answer is not the simple 'yes' the questioner's framing invites: he affirms the retraction of specific errors, but he also calls al-Ashari an imam of the people of the sunnah, says he is rewarded even for his mistakes, and says most of what is ascribed to him is not his. Any excerpt that carries only the retraction misrepresents him. Compare article 534 of this slice, which answers a related question at greater length and states that the errors were four in number.

options: following a scholar in the doctrines of creed is impermissible
following a scholar in the doctrines of creed is barred
following a scholar in the doctrines of creed is ruled out
flags.note: NOTE ON §8. As in article 534, يمتنع here attaches to an act (taqlīd) and is a legal judgement, not the kalām modality mumtaniʿ ('rationally impossible'). The distinction matters in this file because its subject is creed; a later reviser must not re-read the word as the modal term.

translator_notes: Verse and quotation renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.

This article overlaps substantially with article 534 of this slice, which answers a related question. The two are not identical and have been translated independently; 534 states that the errors number four, which this article does not. A reviewer may wish to compare them.

Throughout, the Sheikh distinguishes Abu al-Hasan al-Ashari's own positions from what the later Asharis hold and from what is ascribed to him. Every one of those attributions has been kept visibly distinct in the English, since the whole answer turns on them.

'He has two rewards … he has one reward' renders the formula of the hadith on the judge who exercises his own reasoning; the Sheikh applies it without citing the hadith, and nothing has been supplied.

The lines of verse are rendered as prose in italics per house style; the Arabic should be displayed alongside, since the subject matter is technical and the source's layout of the al-Suyuti lines is itself defective (see the flag).
Source spellings preserved verbatim in body_ar: الإجتهادات with a connecting hamza, الخطإ and موطإه with the hamza on the kasrah seat, and الحافظ بن عساكر for ابن عساكر.
